Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

automatically adverb

also by itself, of its own accord, automatic, without thinking, on its own

classical

Liv. 1.39.2: dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset
Varr. RR 2.9.6

suā sponte

of its own accord, by itself

Of free will, or of one’s own agency without help: of people, animals and things alike. In good prose always with meā, tuā, suā; the poets also write sponte suā and sponte alone (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • per sē — by itself, of itself

    also used · classical

    By itself, without anything else: per sē movētur. Also “in itself” (see the sense of the phrase in each passage).

  • ultrō — unprompted, of one’s own accord

    adverb · also used · classical

    Without being asked, going further than expected; of a person, rarely of a machine.

Examples

  • parce, puer, stimulīs et fortius ūtere lōrīs: sponte suā properant; labor est inhibēre volentēs

    spare the goad, boy, and use the reins more firmly: they hurry of their own accord; the work is holding them back when they want to goOv. Met. 2.127–128

  • movērī vetuisse puerum dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset

    she forbade anyone to move the boy until he woke up by himselfLiv. 1.39.2

  • Jānua suā sponte aperītur.

    The door opens automatically.composed

See also alone.
